source_identity.title: Towards a Standard for Identifying and Managing Bias in Artificial Intelligence

entries.external_proposition: Use disaggregated and context-relevant performance analysis to identify differential impacts that aggregate metrics may conceal.
entries.rationale: Disaggregated performance and differential-impact analysis is a fairness/bias-management practice; the current neutral invariant set does not define fairness as an invariant.

entries.external_proposition: Assign governance responsibility for identifying, assessing, documenting and mitigating AI bias.
entries.rationale: Organisational assignment of accountability is an institutional governance practice outside the current operational invariant set.

entries.external_proposition: Treat AI bias as a socio-technical phenomenon with systemic, computational and human contributors.
entries.rationale: The socio-technical definition explains bias context and does not itself impose a VIGIL invariant.

entries.external_proposition: Feed monitoring, incident and stakeholder information back into dataset, design and risk-treatment decisions.
entries.rationale: Monitoring and stakeholder information informs risk treatment. Lifecycle feedback does not require timely correlation of material runtime signals.

relationships.external_proposition: Feed monitoring, incident and stakeholder information back into dataset, design and risk-treatment decisions.
relationships.fc_property: The property by which individually captured material monitoring, control and execution signals carry sufficient correlation identity and context to be assembled across records, channels and review surfaces within the time needed for relevant oversight or intervention.
relationships.invariant: Signals concerning the same event, pathway, actor, object, or risk must carry sufficient correlation identity and context and reach an integrated review surface in time for required oversight or intervention. Individual capture is insufficient where operationally disconnected signals prevent recognition of the material state.
relationships.supported_component: Monitoring and stakeholder information informs risk treatment.

actors: Individual or group responsible for designing, developing, deploying, evaluating, or governing AI systems
objects: Deployed AI system, bias incidents, user feedback, and organizational bias-management practices
conditions: Feedback and monitoring depend on lawful, privacy-appropriate collection of relevant data and accessible recourse channels.
qualifications: NIST SP 1270 is voluntary recommended practice and does not establish or supersede a law, regulation, legal requirement, or legal defense.
The publication is preliminary guidance and a roadmap for future work; it does not provide a complete procedure or guarantee zero bias.
Zero risk of bias is not achievable, and bias management must account for interacting systemic, statistical or computational, and human factors in context.
Specific measures, metrics, controls, and acceptable residual risk depend on the use case, affected populations, operational context, and applicable legal requirements.

relationships.strength_reason: Monitoring and stakeholder information informs risk treatment. Lifecycle feedback does not require timely correlation of material runtime signals.
relationships.limitation: Lifecycle feedback does not require timely correlation of material runtime signals.

entries.external_proposition: Document evaluation assumptions, uncertainty, limitations and residual bias risks.
entries.rationale: Documented evaluation assumptions, uncertainty and residual bias. Bias assurance documentation does not establish the full decision-specific reliance threshold.

relationships.external_proposition: Document evaluation assumptions, uncertainty, limitations and residual bias risks.
relationships.fc_property: The property by which generated, retrieved, transformed, inferred and synthesised epistemic artefacts receive assurance calibrated to the downstream reliance threshold, including source quality, traceability, independence, uncertainty, temporal fitness and error consequences, while lower-assurance material remains provisional.
relationships.invariant: Before an epistemic artefact is promoted, accepted, or used in a materially consequential decision, its assurance posture must meet the downstream reliance threshold, calibrated to source quality, traceability, independence, uncertainty, temporal fitness, and error consequences. Lower-assurance material must remain provisional.

relationships.external_proposition: Assess bias periodically throughout the AI lifecycle and after contextual, data, model or use changes.
relationships.fc_property: The property by which a prior verification result remains bounded to its verified conditions and is used as current assurance only when continued applicability across material state or contextual changes is independently established.
relationships.invariant: A prior verification may support a later claim only while its applicability to the current time, target, state, version, environment, dependencies, and scope remains established. Otherwise it is historical evidence and the current claim must be revalidated or marked unresolved.
